items.name: the bed of Ulysses
items.description: Marriage bed built round a living olive tree, the secret proving Ulysses' identity to Penelope.

items.name: the bow of Ulysses
items.description: Great bow given to Ulysses by Iphitus; only Ulysses can string it, and he uses it to slaughter the suitors.

items.name: the axes
items.description: Twelve axes set in a row; the bow must shoot through them in the contest.

items.name: Penelope's web
items.description: Shroud for Laertes that Penelope wove by day and unpicked by night to delay the suitors.

items.name: the raft of Ulysses
items.description: Raft Ulysses builds on Calypso's island, wrecked by Neptune's storm.

items.name: the cattle of the Sun
items.description: Sacred cattle on Thrinacia; Ulysses' men slaughter them and are destroyed.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Cattle of Helios, also called the Oxen of the Sun, are cattle pastured on the island of Thrinacia, or Thrinakia (in later sources identified with Sicily).

items.name: the wooden horse
items.description: Hollow horse in which Greek heroes hid to sack Troy; Demodocus sings of it.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Trojan Horse was a wooden horse said to have been used by the Greeks during the Trojan War to sneak into the city of Troy and win the war. The Trojan Horse is not mentioned in Homer's Iliad, with the poem ending before the war is concluded, and it is only briefly mentioned in the Odyssey.

items.name: the herb Moly
items.description: Herb given by Mercury to Ulysses that protects him against Circe's drugs.

items.name: Ino's veil
items.description: Divine veil Ino gives Ulysses to keep him afloat after Neptune wrecks his raft.

items.name: Maron's wine
items.description: Strong wine given to Ulysses that he uses to make Polyphemus drunk.

items.name: the aegis
items.description: Minerva's terrifying shield, which sends the suitors fleeing in the final battle.

wikipedia.lead: The aegis or egis, as stated in the Iliad, is a device carried by Zeus, Apollo and Athena, variously interpreted as an animal skin or a shield and sometimes featuring the head of a Gorgon. There may be a connection with a deity named Aex, a daughter of Helios and a nurse of Zeus or alternatively a mistress of Zeus (Hyginus, Astronomica 2.

items.name: the bag of winds
items.description: Ox-hide sack of winds given by Aeolus; Ulysses' men open it within sight of Ithaca.

items.name: the stake of Ulysses
items.description: Sharpened olive stake used to blind Polyphemus.
